newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rates big Ford tops for side impact protection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rates big Ford tops for side impact protection.

text.p: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Friday issued the first in a series of side-crash test results, and rated the Ford Motor Co. Crown Victoria 4-door as the safest.
Previously, the NHTSA only rated cars for passenger protection from frontal crashes.
The NHTSA, rating cars on a scale from one to five stars, with five the best, gave the Crown Victoria four stars for both front and rear seat passenger protection.
No car of the 17 tested was given five-stars.
Public Citizen and Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety applauded the NHTSA action.

Public Citizen president Joan Claybrook said that car makers tried to block the programme, but fortunately it was supported by Representative Frank Wolf, a Republican of Virginia who is chairman of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation.
Claybrook, a former NHTSA administrator, said the additional data will prove valuable for consumers making decisions about which car to buy.
The ratings should encourage manufacturers to improve side impact protection on their autos, she said.
The NHTSA said cars with four stars for either front or rear seat protection, but not both, were:

- General Motors Corp. Chevrolet Camaro 2-door, with three stars for the front seat and four for the rear; Chevrolet Lumina 4-door, four stars for the front and three for the rear; and Chrysler Corp. Dodge Intrepid 4-door, four stars for the front and three for the rear.
Cars with the least protection from side crashes:

- Chevrolet Cavalier 2-door, with one star for the front and two for the rear; GMC's Pontiac Gran Am 4-door, one star for the front and three for the rear; Chevrolet Malibu 4-door, with one star for the front and three for the rear; and Ford Thunderbird, with three stars for the front and one for the rear.
